label: mid/late original-phase input of v/e/u/x/h/i/d/m/j in sequences starting with q/l/y/a/p/2/1
explanation: Fires only during the original (input) phase at positions t=3..8, never at t<3, at <DEL>, or in the copy phase. The input at the active step is almost always one of v (strongest, 27% of mass), e, u, x, h, i, then weaker d, m, j; it essentially never fires on s, t or most other tokens. It is gated by sequence context: much more likely when the first original token is q (4.9x), l, y, a, 2, p or 1, and suppressed when v/e/u/x/h/i-type tokens already appeared at positions 1-2 (adding that condition raises precision to 0.59 but cuts recall to 0.55). It is mostly the first occurrence of the input token (92% of mass), but a repeated token right after its first occurrence can also fire. The top activations (v after q-initial prefixes such as y q p a k 3 v) fit this pattern. Precision is limited (about 0.38 on dev) because the token and context conditions only raise the firing probability; activation looks like a graded readout of the earlier prefix that one boolean cannot capture.
